verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Routine rewriting, two steps. (i) The Lean works in Vec2 = Fin 2 → ℝ and packs the two covariance vectors as the columns of H : Mat2; H.mulVec c = c 0 • (column 0) + c 1 • (column 1) by Fin.sum_univ_two, so `reconstruct` with c = weights H T is literally T = c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ with the sides swapped. (ii) The paper's `c₁, c₂ > 0` is `StrictCone.weights_pos`; `weights_pos_iff` (line 60) makes the two exactly equivalent, so the Lean's StrictCone predicate is precisely the paper's `T lies in the interior of the cone generated by v₁, v₂`. The paper's side condition T ≠ 0 is not written as a hypothesis in Lean but is implied by StrictCone: at T = 0 the cramerNumerator is ![0,0], so `0 < 0 * H.det` fails. `reconstruct_amplitudes` gives the same identity with c_i = (amplitude_i)², matching the paper's phrase about fluxes per unit squared amplitude, and `amplitudes_pos` (line 97) gives their positivity. The content is split over `reconstruct` (the identity, which needs only H.det ≠ 0) and `StrictCone.weights_pos` (the positivity); conjoining them is one line.
